description: Heatmap of the reasons Australian owners gave for getting each type of pet, Animal Medicines Australia survey 2025. Only each pet's top five reasons were published; other cells are hatched as not published.

title.description: The big heading and the smaller line under it. On a phone the words are split into shorter lines.

text.signal: narrow ? ['Companionship leads, except', 'for fish and reptiles'] : 'Companionship leads, except for fish and reptiles'

subtitle.signal: narrow ? ['Share of owners giving each reason for', 'getting their pet, 2025'] : 'Share of owners giving each reason for getting their pet, 2025'

usermeta.readMe: Vega ignores this box. It holds plain-language notes for the parts of the chart that cannot carry their own "description".
usermeta.config: Default look for every axis in this chart: no axis line, no tick marks, no gridlines, and a small gap between the words and the squares.

scales.x: Gives each pet its own column, from left to right, after the room kept for reason names.
scales.y: Gives each reason its own row, in the fixed reading order set by "reasonOrder" (companionship first). Percentages from different pets are not added up to sort the rows.
scales.colour: Turns a percentage into a colour: palest brown for 0%, darkest brown for 60%. Darker means more owners gave that reason.
scales.petColour: Gives each pet its fixed colour, used for the pet names along the top.

usermeta.codeGuide: Signals set the responsive layout and theme. Data transforms derive values; scales map them to positions and colours; marks draw the chart.

signals.name: colorMuted
signals.description: Colour: the dark grey colour of small text: labels, axis words and notes. This is only a backup; the real colour comes from --color-muted in css/style.css.

signals.name: colorHeading
signals.description: Colour: the dark blue colour of chart titles. This is only a backup; the real colour comes from --color-heading in css/style.css.

signals.name: colorLight
signals.description: Colour: the palest brown, used for the smallest numbers on a colour scale. This is only a backup; the real colour comes from --color-light in css/style.css.

signals.name: colorDark
signals.description: Colour: the darkest brown, used for the biggest numbers on a colour scale. This is only a backup; the real colour comes from --color-dark in css/style.css.

signals.name: colorBorder
signals.description: Colour: light grey, used for gridlines, empty squares and places with no data. This is only a backup; the real colour comes from --color-border in css/style.css.

signals.name: colorSurface
signals.description: Colour: white, the colour of the card each chart sits on. This is only a backup; the real colour comes from --color-surface in css/style.css.

signals.name: colorPetDogs
signals.description: Colour: the colour for dogs (amber). This is only a backup; the real colour comes from --color-pet-dogs in css/style.css.

signals.name: colorPetCats
signals.description: Colour: the colour for cats (plum). This is only a backup; the real colour comes from --color-pet-cats in css/style.css.

signals.name: colorPetFish
signals.description: Colour: the colour for fish (teal). This is only a backup; the real colour comes from --color-pet-fish in css/style.css.

signals.name: colorPetBirds
signals.description: Colour: the colour for birds (green). This is only a backup; the real colour comes from --color-pet-birds in css/style.css.

signals.name: colorPetSmallMammals
signals.description: Colour: the colour for small mammals (violet). This is only a backup; the real colour comes from --color-pet-small-mammals in css/style.css.

signals.name: colorPetReptiles
signals.description: Colour: the colour for reptiles (raspberry). This is only a backup; the real colour comes from --color-pet-reptiles in css/style.css.

signals.name: colorPetOther
signals.description: Colour: the colour for other pets (grey). This is only a backup; the real colour comes from --color-pet-other in css/style.css.

signals.name: fontHeading
signals.description: Font: the fancy title font (DM Serif Display). This is only a backup; the real font comes from --font-heading in css/style.css.

signals.name: fontBody
signals.description: Font: the plain font for all other text (Fira Sans). This is only a backup; the real font comes from --font-body in css/style.css.

signals.name: width
signals.description: How wide the chart is. It starts as the width of the box on the page and updates whenever the browser window is resized.

signals.name: narrow
signals.description: True when the chart is less than 760 pixels wide (for example on a phone). Other parts check it to use shorter words, upright pet names and a stacked key.

signals.name: labelWidth
signals.description: How much room is kept on the left for the reason names.

signals.name: rowHeight
signals.description: How tall each row of squares is.

signals.name: gridHeight
signals.description: How tall the whole grid of squares is: 11 reasons times the row height.

signals.name: height
signals.description: How tall the whole chart is: the grid plus room underneath for the key.

signals.name: legendY
signals.description: How far down the key starts: just under the grid.

data.name: published
data.description: The survey numbers: for each pet, the share of owners who gave each reason. Only each pet's top five reasons were published.

transform.description: Make a joined-up key like "Dogs|Companionship", so each square can find its number.

data.name: owners
data.description: How many owners of each pet were asked (used in the pop-up box).

transform.description: Find how many owners of each pet were asked.

data.name: reasons
data.description: One row per distinct reason. A fixed thematic order avoids treating sums of percentages from different owner groups as a combined prevalence.

transform.description: Keep distinct reason names without summing percentages across species.

transform.expr: indexof(["Companionship","Mental health","Relaxation","Hobby","Lower maintenance","Given/left to me","Breed temperament","Rescue/give a home","Breed size","Eggs","Companion for other pets"], datum.reason)
transform.description: Group motivations in a deliberate reading order, not by a pooled percentage.
Replace short reason names from the file with clearer full words, for example "Breed has a good temperament".
transform.expr: {'Mental health': 'For mental health', 'Given/left to me': 'Given or left to me', 'Breed temperament': 'Breed has a good temperament', 'Rescue/give a home': 'Rescue or give a home', 'Breed size': 'Breed is a suitable size', 'Eggs': 'For their eggs'}[datum.reason] || datum.reason

transform.description: Shorter versions of each reason name, split into two lines, for phones.
transform.expr: {'Companionship': ['Companionship'], 'Mental health': ['For mental', 'health'], 'Relaxation': ['Relaxation'], 'Hobby': ['Hobby'], 'Lower maintenance': ['Lower', 'maintenance'], 'Given/left to me': ['Given or', 'left to me'], 'Breed temperament': ['Good breed', 'temperament'], 'Rescue/give a home': ['Rescue or', 'give a home'], 'Breed size': ['Breed is a', 'suitable size'], 'Eggs': ['For their eggs'], 'Companion for other pets': ['Companion for', 'other pets']}[datum.reason] || [datum.reason]

transform.description: List the six pets, so every reason can be paired with every pet.

data.name: cells
data.description: One row per square in the grid: every reason for every pet, with its number if it was published.

transform.description: Make one row for every reason and pet pair (11 reasons times 6 pets).
Make the same joined-up key, like "Dogs|Companionship".
Look up the published percentage for this pair. If there is none, leave it empty (not zero).
Look up how many owners of this pet were asked.
Mark whether this square has a published number.

data.name: hatchLines
data.description: The short diagonal lines that cross out squares with no published number.

transform.description: Keep only the squares with no published number.
Make a list of starting points, 8 pixels apart, for the diagonal lines.
Make one row per diagonal line.

data.name: legendHatch
data.description: The diagonal lines inside the crossed-out square in the key.

transform.description: Make a list of starting points, 8 pixels apart, for the key's diagonal lines.
Make one row per diagonal line in the key.

range.signal: [colorPetDogs, colorPetCats, colorPetFish, colorPetBirds, colorPetSmallMammals, colorPetReptiles, colorPetOther]

axes.description: The pet names along the top of the grid, each in its pet colour. On a phone they stand upright to fit.

marks.description: The reason names on the left of each row (shorter, two-line names on a phone).
The squares of the grid. Squares with a published number are coloured by it; the others are white.

tooltip.signal: datum.published_cell ? {'Pet type': datum.species, 'Reason': datum.label, 'Owners giving this reason': datum.percent + '%', 'Owners surveyed': format(datum.sample_n, ',.0f'), 'Survey year': 2025} : {'Pet type': datum.species, 'Reason': datum.label, 'Value': 'Not published: outside this pet\'s top five reasons', 'Interpretation': 'An unpublished value is not zero'}

marks.name: motivationCells

marks.description: Diagonal lines over the white squares, to show "not published". Each line is cut to stay inside its square (lines poking out would make the chart shrink).

x.signal: scale('x', datum.species) + max(0, min(datum.offset, bandwidth('x') + bandwidth('y')) - bandwidth('y'))

y.signal: scale('y', datum.reason) + min(min(datum.offset, bandwidth('x') + bandwidth('y')), bandwidth('y'))

x2.signal: scale('x', datum.species) + min(min(datum.offset, bandwidth('x') + bandwidth('y')), bandwidth('x'))

y2.signal: scale('y', datum.reason) + max(0, min(datum.offset, bandwidth('x') + bandwidth('y')) - bandwidth('x'))

marks.description: The colour strip in the key, going from pale to dark.
The words above the colour strip: "Share of owners: 0% to 60%".
The white square in the key that shows what "not published" looks like.
The diagonal lines inside that key square.
The words next to that key square, explaining "not published".

text.signal: narrow ? ['Not published: outside', 'this pet\'s top five'] : 'Not published: outside this pet\'s top five reasons'

marks.description: Print every published percentage; unpublished cells remain hatched.

tooltip.signal: datum.published_cell ? {'Pet type': datum.species, 'Reason': datum.label, 'Owners giving this reason': datum.percent + '%', 'Owners surveyed': format(datum.sample_n, ',.0f'), 'Survey year': 2025} : {'Pet type': datum.species, 'Reason': datum.label, 'Value': 'Not published: outside this pet\'s top five reasons', 'Interpretation': 'An unpublished value is not zero'}

marks.name: motivationValues
